module purpose: neorv32_cpu_counters decodes CSR accesses from ctrl_i to read or update cycle, instret, and configurable HPM counters plus HPM event-selection registers. It computes per-counter increment enables from ctrl_i event/debug/halt fields, instantiates counter blocks, and returns the selected counter or configuration word on rdata_o.

use-case flows.value: HPM event-selection mask bits written from ctrl_i.csr_wdata into hpmevent(i) when an HPM configuration CSR write is decoded
per-counter increment-enable decisions captured in cnt_en from ctrl_i.cnt_event, ctrl_i.cpu_debug, ctrl_i.cnt_halt, and hpmevent(i), then driven into counter instances
counter low and high words updated either by CSR write data or by increment and carry accumulation in each neorv32_cpu_counters_cnt instance
selected counter words and selected HPM event-selection values returned through rdata_o
cnt_en, hpmevent, and counter registers cleared to zero while rstn_i = '0'

conceptual assets.concept: Per-CSR access strobes deciding which counter or HPM-event register is read or written
conceptual assets.reasoning: Lines 82-86 derive per-index select and strobes from ctrl_i: sel(i) from csr_addr low bits (82), cnt_we(i)/cnt_re(i) from cnt_acc and sel(i) with csr_we/csr_re (83-84), and cfg_we(i)/cfg_re(i) from cfg_acc and sel(i) with csr_we/csr_re (85-86). Lines 90-94 qualify the counter and HPM-event address ranges. These decisions drive counter sub-unit we_i/re_i ports (133-134, 152-153, 187-188) and gate hpmevent update and readback (199, 223). Integrity is established because the configure and read-out flows depend on writes and reads reaching only the addressed target; availability is also established because, when the decoded address and csr_we/csr_re match, the corresponding strobe vector is produced.

Process cnt_control stores cnt_en: bit 0 takes `ctrl_i.cnt_event(cnt_event_cy_c) and (not ctrl_i.cpu_debug) and (not ctrl_i.cnt_halt(0))` at line 108, bit 2 takes the instruction-retire condition at line 110, and bits 3 to 15 take `or_reduce_f(ctrl_i.cnt_event and hpmevent(i)) and (not ctrl_i.cpu_debug) and (not ctrl_i.cnt_halt(i))` at line 112. These decisions are then delivered to counter-instance inc_i ports at lines 131, 150, and 185. Integrity is established because the counter-update flow depends on increments occurring only under those predicates; availability is also established because, with reset inactive, cnt_en is updated every clock in lines 102-115 and consumed by enabled counter instances.

conceptual assets.concept: HPM event-selection masks that choose which events increment each HPM counter
conceptual assets.reasoning: Under `ZIHPM_EN and (HPM_NUM > 0)`, hpmevent_reg resets hpmevent(i) to zero (196-197), writes `ctrl_i.csr_wdata(11 downto 0)` when `cfg_we(i) = '1'` (199-200), and then forces `hpmevent(i)(cnt_event_tm_c) <= '0'` (202). The stored mask is consumed in the HPM cnt_en computation at line 112 and is read back when `cfg_re(i) = '1'` through lines 223-227 and top output line 97. Integrity is established because both HPM event selection and configuration readback depend on the exact stored bits; availability is also established because the mask is held between writes and returned on matching reads. When `(not ZIHPM_EN) or (HPM_NUM = 0)`, hpmevent is tied to zero instead (236-237).

conceptual assets.concept: Stored counter values returned by the cycle, instret, and enabled HPM counters
conceptual assets.reasoning: In each neorv32_cpu_counters_cnt instance, lo_q resets to zero (299-300), loads wdata_i on a low-word write (302-303), otherwise takes the incremented nxt value (305, 311-312). When `CNT_WIDTH > 32`, hi_q resets to zero (320-322), loads wdata_i on a high-word write (325-326), otherwise accumulates carry from cy_q (324, 328). output_select returns the selected low or high word on reads (345-349). The top module exposes cycle and instret counter read data when `ZICNTR_EN` (124-156) and HPM counter read data when `ZIHPM_EN and (HPM_NUM > 0)` (178-190, 216-227), then drives `rdata_o <= cycle_rd or time_rd or instret_rd or hpm_rd;` at line 97; disabled builds tie the corresponding outputs to zero at lines 163-165 and 235-237. Integrity is established because counting, explicit CSR writes, and readout all depend on these stored values; availability is also established because the counter state is preserved between updates and delivered on selected reads.
